Police believe a man started a fire in a locked room, killing himself and seriously injuring others in a house at the Gold Coast overnight.

Two men – a 44-year-old and an 84-year-old – were woken by crackling in a locked room, and attempted to break the door down but suffered life-threatening injuries before escaping.

Emergency teams were called to the burning residence on Sickle Avenue at Hope Island about 11.45pm on Tuesday.

They were taken to the Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital.

A 59-year-old woman and 38-year-old man escaped by jumping out a window. The woman suffered a back injury, and was taken to the same hospital.

A man was later found dead inside the home.

Detective Superintendent Chris Ahern confirmed some people in the house were family members, and officers had been called to the address a week earlier over alleged threats.

“It highlights the fragility in human relationships and we send the message any violence is unacceptable,” Ahern said.

He added the man who died was yet to be formally identified.

Investigations at the scene were ongoing at midday on Wednesday, with officers calling for anyone who witnessed the fire or had further information to come forward.
